sources.author: Swyx
sources.headline: Developer at AWS & AI Community Builder
sources.post_summary: Discusses the evolution of AI agents from hype to practical multi-agent systems, sharing insights on frameworks like LangGraph and AutoGen for building reliable agent workflows. Emphasizes the need for better developer tools to handle agent orchestration and debugging. Highlights real-world applications in automation beyond chatbots.

sources.author: Andrej Karpathy
sources.headline: Founder at Eureka Labs, ex-OpenAI
sources.post_summary: Explores the infrastructure challenges in scaling AI agents, including compute demands and data pipelines for training agentic systems. Shares thoughts on why current developer tools fall short for agent simulation and testing. Predicts a shift towards agent-first AI infrastructure in the coming year.

sources.author: Hamel Husain
sources.headline: Independent AI Researcher
sources.post_summary: Breaks down advanced techniques for building production-ready AI agents using open-source tools like LlamaIndex and CrewAI. Focuses on automation patterns for code generation and multi-step reasoning. Provides code snippets and benchmarks for developer adoption.

sources.author: Nat Friedman
sources.headline: Co-founder at GitHub (former)
sources.post_summary: Analyzes the rise of AI infrastructure platforms like Together AI and Pinecone for powering agent fleets. Discusses integration with developer tools for seamless automation pipelines. Shares investment perspectives on the next wave of AI infra startups.

sources.author: Addy Osmani
sources.headline: Engineering Leader at Google Chrome
sources.post_summary: Details how web developers can leverage AI agents for browser automation and testing using tools like Playwright with LLM integrations. Covers performance implications and best practices for AI-driven dev workflows. Includes a demo repo for hands-on experimentation.

sources.author: Sami Rahman
sources.headline: Founder @ RevGenius | GTM Engineering Expert
sources.post_summary: Discusses building scalable GTM engines by integrating engineering with sales processes. Shares a framework for automating outbound at scale while maintaining personalization. Emphasizes data-driven iteration for revenue growth.

sources.author: Amy Volas
sources.headline: CEO @ Avenue Talent Partners | Sales Leadership Advisor
sources.post_summary: Explores the evolution of sales ops into revenue operations, highlighting key metrics and tools for alignment. Provides actionable steps for sales ops leaders to transition to RevOps roles. Warns against common pitfalls in outbound automation implementation.

sources.author: Arvid Kahl
sources.headline: Author & Serial Entrepreneur | bootstrapped to $50M ARR
sources.post_summary: Outlines a content strategy playbook for B2B SaaS GTM, focusing on audience-first creation and distribution. Details how to leverage LinkedIn for organic lead gen without heavy ad spend. Includes case studies from his own ventures.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: Head of Sales @ Lavender | Sales Tech Investor
sources.post_summary: Breaks down outbound automation myths and shares a tested tech stack for high-volume prospecting. Focuses on AI-driven personalization to boost reply rates in sales ops. Provides ROI benchmarks from enterprise implementations.

sources.author: Dan Khan
sources.headline: Fractional CRO | Revenue Operations Consultant
sources.post_summary: Presents a RevOps maturity model for aligning sales, marketing, and customer success. Covers GTM engineering principles for mid-market SaaS. Shares templates for content strategy integration into revenue flywheels.

sources.author: Pieter Levels
sources.headline: Indie Maker & Founder of Nomad List, Remote OK
sources.post_summary: Pieter shares his journey as a solo developer shipping multiple products like Nomad List and Remote OK without VC funding. He emphasizes the power of building in public, iterating based on user feedback, and achieving profitability through bootstrapping. His post inspires others to start small and ship fast.

sources.author: Arvid Kahl
sources.headline: Serial Entrepreneur, Author of Zero to Sold
sources.post_summary: Arvid recounts bootstrapping and selling his SaaS company FeedbackPanda for 7 figures as a solo founder. He details the process of shipping MVPs, marketing on Twitter and LinkedIn, and building in public to attract acquirers. The post offers practical advice for solo builders aiming for acquisition.

sources.author: KP (Karthik Rajagopalan)
sources.headline: Founder of SuperHi, Ex-Head of Design at Twitter
sources.post_summary: KP shares his career pivot from design at big tech to founding SuperHi, a no-code platform for creators. He discusses the challenges of going solo, shipping the product in public, and lessons on product-market fit. The post motivates career switchers into tech entrepreneurship.

sources.author: Daniel Vassallo
sources.headline: Ex-AWS, Indie Maker & Writer
sources.post_summary: Daniel details his pivot from Amazon engineer to solo indie maker, shipping small products like PDFtoKeynote that generate passive income. He advocates for building in public to validate ideas quickly and shares revenue updates transparently. His approach highlights sustainable solo development.

sources.author: Courtland Allen
sources.headline: Founder of Indie Hackers
sources.post_summary: Courtland reflects on building Indie Hackers as a side project before pivoting full-time into tech entrepreneurship. He stresses shipping publicly, engaging the community for feedback, and scaling without a team. The post is a blueprint for solo founders in the maker movement.
